limitations: Not every live session runs 1.15.0 yet, and nothing in the claim rests on that. At the cutover read-back 12 already-running 1.14.0 servers remained; at 2026-09-28T02:03:14Z a process listing still showed 2 processes on the 1.14.0 prefix, the MCP children of two long-running Claude Code sessions that each need their own /mcp reconnect. A codebase_graph_status read-back at about 02:07Z, served by one of those 1.14.0 servers, showed the stored graph still 'Built by: v1.15.0' (last built 2026-09-27T21:43:08.450Z). A 1.14.0 server that rebuilds the graph before its session reconnects would restart the flip-flop (data.all_sessions_on_1150).

The pre-cutover checks ran from the staged 1.15.0 prefix against production services while 1.14.0 servers were still running, and shared their lock directory. The 1.15.0 server rebuilt the production code graph ('Built by: v1.15.0', last built 2026-09-27T21:34:21.531Z); a 1.14.0 server rebuilt it again at 21:35:09.670Z, as the post-cutover graph status shows. The decision record predicted this graph flip-flop from source (graph-inputs.ts:609); this is the first native observation of it on this host. No vector reindex was observed: the collection stayed green at 89,567 chunks throughout.

Evidence classes differ by part. The upstream suite is the unchanged upstream test code at the tag, with the deviations in data.upstream_suite.deviations. The client checks are local integration evidence, one run per client; the Claude probe ran on claude-haiku-4-5 as a connectivity check, and its model does not change the server's behaviour. The cutover and its read-back are native operations by the coordinator: the mcporter read-backs quote retained captures, while the claude mcp get and codex mcp get results are the coordinator's reported observations, whose raw output is not retained. The 2026-09-25 qualification is documented in docs/decisions/2026-09-25-workstation-sota-refresh.md, but its artifacts were never published, so it is not cited as output here.

The Codex check needed default_tools_approval_mode="approve": socraticode declares no MCP tool annotations, and `codex exec` runs with approval policy never, so an unapproved call is refused (docs/decisions/2026-09-26-codex-worker-lane.md, decisions 4 and 5). This is not a 1.15.0 change: the src/tools tree is 7044488e at both tags, so tool names and parameters are unchanged.

The upstream suite does not cover everything upstream CI runs. Node 24.21.0 is outside the CI unit matrix (18/20/22/26), and the Qdrant job runs on Node 26. Qdrant 1.19.1 replaced CI's v1.17.0. npm run build was skipped before the regressions, because no test references dist/. Not run: the Docker-backed test:integration and test:e2e suites (this host has no Docker), the rust-graph-vs-cargo job, and the packaged-artifact consumer jobs. npm ci warned that 19 packages have install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts, and its audit reported 3 moderate severity vulnerabilities; neither was reviewed here.

The sha256 pin covers socraticode's own tarball only. The package ships no shrinkwrap, and later releases inside its dependency ranges now resolve: undici 6.29.0 (2026-09-25T09:45:19.865Z) and @lumis-sh/wasm-eex 0.26.2 (2026-09-26T00:38:34.735Z). recipes/README.md therefore installs with --before=2026-09-24T12:00:00Z. adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh install_npm passes no --before, so a bootstrap install can resolve a different dependency tree from the qualified one.

The landscape ledger does not move: catalogs/landscape/foundation.json keeps the winner pin socraticode 1.14.0 from the sealed 2026-09-22 layer-verdict packets (decision record, Scope). A host receipt recorded at 1.15.0 therefore matches no winner pin. scripts/host_receipts.py record refuses it unless --allow-unbound-version is passed, and it stays unbound until a new verdict wave re-records the layer.
Linux x86_64 only: adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json keeps socraticode 1.14.0. The npm tarball is platform-independent, but a Mac needs its own acceptance, and nothing here is macOS evidence.

The user waived the recorded 7-day cooldown (earliest cutover 2026-10-01T11:01Z), so it was not served; the release was about 3.4 days old at the decision. The upstream check at 2026-09-27T21:45Z found no newer release, main 9 commits ahead with documentation changes only, and no issue reporting a 1.15.0 regression. That rules out only regressions already reported.

Not repointed: 16 ephemeral scratch CODEX_HOMEs under other sessions' scratchpads, plus dated backups and archived documents. The scratch homes are live launchers, not history: a dated reviewer observation (PR #446 review, 2026-09-28) found a peer session's scratch Codex review home whose config.toml was created at 2026-09-27T22:37:21Z, 54 min after the cutover, from main's pre-merge template, and names tools/socraticode-1.14.0. Such homes keep launching 1.14.0 until this change merges and they are re-rendered, and each such server can rebuild the shared graph as 1.14.0, restarting the flip-flop in the first limitation.

The notifications/message counts are untested (no discriminating control): the zero matches in data.pre_cutover_native and data.post_cutover_readback come from captures with no failing control of the same predicate, so docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md records them as untested and the claim does not rest on them.

Not exercised: interactive sessions over time with the newly delivered notifications/message stream, beyond the single calls here (its volume at SOCRATICODE_LOG_LEVEL info); the mcporter daemon keep-alive path under load; and the two mixed-session hazards known from source only, the cross-process symbol-graph staging cleanup race (symbol-graph-store.ts:843-866, startup.ts:324-336) and codebase_stop's SIGTERM to another session's indexer (index-tools.ts:478-499).
